spec.name: Bauhaus Songbird on a Branch
spec.description: A stylized songbird assembled from pure circles, half-circles, triangles and bars in hard red, yellow, blue, black and cream, perched on a felled branch resting on the floor.
spec.layout: Model space: +Y up, bird faces +Z, centred on x=0. The ground line is a straight felled branch of radius about 0.085 lying along Z from z=-0.95 to z=+0.88, centre line at y=0.09, so its lowest points touch y=0; its front end (z=+0.88) is a flat cut face showing concentric growth-ring discs, its rear end is a rough broken taper, and a knobbly side twig rises from the branch's left-rear (+X side) at z=-0.35 up to y about 0.46, carrying three flat geometric leaves (a blue circle, a yellow half-disc, a red triangle) and small yellow bud spheres. The bird perches on top of the branch at z=+0.05, feet gripping the branch top at y=0.175: an egg-shaped blue torso (centre about [0, 0.42, 0.04], about 0.14 x 0.185 x 0.17, chest tilted slightly forward) with a bold red half-disc breast plate on its front, a cream lower belly bulge, and a black rump band; a round black head (r about 0.095) at [0, 0.66, 0.17] with a cream cheek patch, large side eyes (white ring, black pupil, both visible from the front), a yellow triangular beak pointing forward-down to z about 0.34, and a tiny blue crest wedge; folded black wings as flat slabs hugging each flank from the shoulders (x about plus/minus 0.13, y 0.53) down-back to pointed tips near [x, 0.34, -0.30], each wearing a white bar and a yellow bar near the trailing edge with three stepped primary tips; a fan tail of five flat feather slabs sloping down-back from the rump at [0, 0.45, -0.10] to z about -0.55, blue with a black base band and yellow tips; thin black legs from the belly down to the perch with three forward toes and one rear toe wrapping the branch. The Bauhaus style shows everywhere: every piece is a pure primitive silhouette (spheres, cones, cylinders, extruded circles, half-discs and triangles), every colour a hard flat fill, seams and outlines are thin black parts seated on the surface, and the primaries red-yellow-blue carry the bird while wood browns stay quiet beneath it.

parts.builds: The felled branch and everything on it. Main log: a tapered cylinder (radius 0.095 at the rear end down to 0.075 at the front) along Z from z=-0.95 to z=+0.88, axis at y=0.09 so the bark rests on the floor; wood colour, flat-shaded. Front cut face: a flat disc of woodCut closing the tube at z=+0.88 facing +Z, with two thinner concentric discs stepped slightly forward (woodDark inner, woodCut again, radii about 0.05 and 0.03) reading as growth rings, plus a tiny black centre dot. Rear end tapers to a rough broken stub with a woodDark cap. Two knuckle bulges (slightly flattened woodDark spheres, r about 0.05) embedded in the bark at z=-0.6 and z=+0.4, and 6 small cream lichen dots (flattened spheres r 0.015-0.025) scattered on the upper surface between z=-0.8 and z=+0.7, avoiding the perch point at z=+0.05. Side twig: a rod of radius 0.03 from [0.10, 0.11, -0.35] rising to [0.22, 0.46, -0.30] with a short sub-twig forking to [0.30, 0.40, -0.20], woodDark; on its tips three flat geometric leaves as thin extruded shapes (thickness about 0.012): a blue circle-leaf (r 0.07), a yellow half-disc-leaf (r 0.08, flat edge toward the twig), and a red triangle-leaf (about 0.12 tall), each tilted at a different angle, plus 5 small yellow bud spheres (r 0.018) dotted along the twig. All branch geometry rides the root joint; the twig tips stay under y=0.55 and x under 0.32.
parts.attaches: Rests on the floor by itself (floor: true). The bird's feet land on its top surface at mount perchTop [0, 0.175, 0.05]; leave that spot clear of lichen and knuckles.

parts.builds: The bird's egg body. A blue sphere scaled to an egg (about 0.14 x 0.185 x 0.17 radii) centred at [0, 0.42, 0.04], tilted so the chest sits low at the front (z about +0.19, y about 0.34) and the rump high at the back (z about -0.11, y about 0.50). Breast: a bold red half-disc (extruded half-circle, thickness about 0.035, flat edge down) seated on the front of the chest at about [0, 0.40, 0.165], radius 0.10, arc on top, facing +Z so it reads as a robin-like bib from the front. Lower belly: a cream sphere (r about 0.115) at [0, 0.33, 0.06] bulging out under the chest between the legs. Rump: a thin black band (a short tube or torus segment) round the rear of the egg at about [0, 0.46, -0.09] where it meets the tail mount. Shoulder line: two small blue dome caps (r 0.05) at the wing mounts [plus/minus 0.13, 0.53, 0.08] so the wings seat into the body. A few black seam dots (r 0.008) in a row along the top of the back for rhythm. Torso rides the body joint; keep the belly bottom above y=0.26 since the legs bridge the gap to the branch.
parts.attaches: Feet land on the branch at mount perchTop via the legs part; rear meets the tail at mount tailRoot [0, 0.45, -0.10]; top meets the head at mount neckBase [0, 0.56, 0.12]; wings bolt onto the shoulders at wingShoulderL and wingShoulderR.

parts.builds: The round black head and its face. Skull: a black sphere r 0.095 centred at [0, 0.66, 0.17], tilted slightly forward. Cheek patch: a cream flat disc (extruded circle, thickness 0.015, radius 0.055) seated on each side of the head below and behind the eye at about [plus/minus 0.075, 0.63, 0.15], facing outward. Eyes: on each side at [plus/minus 0.082, 0.68, 0.20] a white sphere (r 0.028) with a black pupil sphere (r 0.015) seated forward on it; both eyes placed far enough forward that they read from the front. Brow accents: two tiny yellow wedge bars above each eye. Beak: a yellow cone (base radius 0.032, length 0.10) from the beak base at [0, 0.64, 0.245] pointing forward and slightly down to a tip at about [0, 0.625, 0.34]; a thin black seam rod (r 0.004) runs along the mouth line from base to tip splitting upper and lower mandible, and the lower mandible is a separate thinner yellow cone (base r 0.024, length 0.08) under the seam so the jaw can open, riding the jaw joint. Crest: one small blue triangle wedge (extruded, about 0.05 tall) standing on the crown at [0, 0.75, 0.14], leaning back. All head geometry rides the head joint except the lower mandible on the jaw joint.
parts.attaches: Sits on the torso at mount neckBase [0, 0.56, 0.12]; the skull's underside overlaps the torso's top so there is no gap.

parts.builds: Both folded wings, mirrored left and right. Each wing is a flat teardrop slab (extruded leaf shape, thickness about 0.035, smoothing 2) rooted at its shoulder mount [plus/minus 0.13, 0.53, 0.08] and laid flat against the flank, sweeping down and back to a pointed tip near [plus/minus 0.10, 0.34, -0.30], black. On each wing near the trailing edge: a cream/white bar (thin extruded strip crossing the wing, about 0.02 thick, seated just proud of the black surface) and a yellow bar below it near the tip, so two hard colour stripes band the folded wing. At the tip, three stepped primary feather slabs (thin flat quads, about 0.09 long, thickness 0.015, staggered 0.02 apart) in blueDark poking past the black tip in a staircase, echoing the Bauhaus rhythm. A thin blue-dark edge line (thin rod or strip) traces the wing's leading edge from shoulder to wrist. Both wings ride the body joint rigidly; keep them inside x = plus/minus 0.26 and clear of the tail slabs.
parts.attaches: Rooted on the torso's shoulders at mount wingShoulderL [0.13, 0.53, 0.08] and wingShoulderR [-0.13, 0.53, 0.08], with the wing root buried slightly into the torso egg so no gap shows; tips reach back over the tail root without touching the tail slabs.

parts.builds: The fanned tail: five flat feather slabs (thin extruded shapes, thickness about 0.016) fanning from the mount tailRoot [0, 0.45, -0.10] down and back to tips around z about -0.52 to -0.58, y about 0.28-0.32; the centre slab is longest, the outer two shorter and angled about 12-18 degrees each side, so the fan reads as a clean triangle silhouette. Each feather is blue with a black band (a thin black slab across the feather's base third) and a yellow tip band (a thin slab across the last 15% of its length); the underside-facing edges can take cream tips on the two outermost feathers. A small black wedge (the rump coverts) caps the fan's root where it meets the torso's rump band. All tail geometry rides the tail joint.
parts.attaches: Rooted into the torso at mount tailRoot [0, 0.45, -0.10], passing just under the wing tips; stays clear of the branch surface (its lowest point around y=0.24, above the branch top of y about 0.175).

parts.builds: The legs and feet that grip the perch. Each leg: a thin black cylinder (r 0.012) from the belly at [plus/minus 0.05, 0.30, 0.05] straight down to the branch top at [plus/minus 0.05, 0.185, 0.05], landing exactly on mount perchTop, with a tiny yellow ring band (thin torus, r 0.014) as an anklet just above the foot. Each foot: three forward toes as short bent rods (r 0.008, about 0.05 long each) spreading at about -35, 0 and +35 degrees around the front of the branch and curling down its sides to about y=0.10, plus one rear toe rod curling back around the branch's underside at z about 0.0, all black with tiny cream claw tips (small cones, 0.012 long). The toes visibly wrap the branch so the grip reads from the front. Leg geometry rides the legL and legR joints; toes ride their own leg's joint.
parts.attaches: Feet land on the branch's top at mount perchTop [0, 0.175, 0.05]; thighs emerge from the torso's cream belly at about y=0.30, buried slightly into the egg so no gap shows.
